title: route reads its walk order from the nest
intention: Route's walk order comes out of its nest: one postprocess sieve, walk_rank, stamps each survivor with (0 if the domain prefers its model else 1, its cash_per_mtoken), route builds survivors from the shake's order, and the two sorts after the shake are deleted; the survivor set and its order stay what they are today.
why: Measured 2026-11-10: route() shakes the nest for cuts only and orders the survivors after it (route.py:293 survivors.sort by cash_per_mtoken; :301 the domain prefers reorder). Akien 2026-09-15: 'capabilities checked first then the post process picked the cheapest ... if it's not like that now, that's a bug'; and 2026-09-29 (open-8ecde12362d6): 'i really like option c' — the shake ranks instead of cutting, and route reads the walk order from the stamps (outline 11.4.6).
traces_to: Outline 11.4.6 (cheapest survivor first; the shake ranks, route reads the walk order from the stamps) and 16.2.3.1; Law 1.
how: Add walk_rank(view, stamps) to SIEVES in route.py (phase_of derives band 2 from stamps); every subject view carries the domain's prefers; route's fire hands band 2 its stamps; survivors are built in shaken['order']; delete survivors.sort at :293 and :301. Red-first proof pins survivors against a frozen copy of the old sort-and-reorder.

clauses.claim: route.py contains no .sort( call and no sorted( call, and import_sieve.phase_of derives band 2 for walk_rank

over a fixture table (cost ties, a preferred model surviving, a preferred model cut, one survivor, the authored stacks; each with no domain, general, and a preferring domain) route's survivors equal, element for element, a frozen copy of the old stable cost sort then stable prefers reorder over the same stacks
walk_rank changes no survivor set: the survivors are exactly the subjects the measure band rolls up to 1.0
every tooth in test_route.py passes unchanged, the walk teeth included
when the measure sieves cut every rung, route raises RouteRefused naming each cut, as today, and an unknown domain still refuses before the shake

decisions.text: D1: cairn/devices/inference_domain/machines/route/route.py: walk_rank(view, stamps) returns (0 if view['combo']['model'] in view['prefers'] else 1, view['provider'].get('cash_per_mtoken')) and joins SIEVES; it reads no other subject, so stamps is the band-2 argument the nest hands it. route() looks the domain row up before the shake (the unknown-domain refusal unchanged) and puts prefers ([] with no domain) in every subject view. The fire is lambda name, view, stamps=None: SIEVES[name](view) if stamps is None else SIEVES[name](view, stamps). Survivors are built by walking shaken['order'] (ties fall to the subject key, which is the combos-stack index, so authored order stays the tiebreak). The two sorts go and the docstring says the order is the nest's.

D2: the proof cairn/devices/inference_domain/machines/route/proofs/test_route_reads_its_walk_order_from_the_nest.py, red-first, PROVES {'ae6bdf48b76d': {'1': 'route_sorts_nothing', '2': 'the_walk_order_is_byte_identical', '3': 'the_rank_cuts_nothing', '4': 'the_standing_teeth_hold', '5': 'refusals_unchanged'}}; tooth 2 holds the old ordering inline as the frozen reference; tooth 4 runs cairn/devices/inference_domain/machines/route/proofs/test_route.py main() in a subprocess; the house runner.

out: cairn/devices/inference_domain/host.py's walk (reads survivors in order, unchanged)
